method: Small AR drafter proposes gamma tokens; target scores them in one pass; modified rejection sampling
upside: Target verifies gamma tokens in one memory-bound pass, so latency drops with no change to the output distribution
method_downside: Separate drafter runs gamma sequential passes and keeps its own KV cache; drafter must share the target tokenizer; rejected tokens waste target FLOPs (more total arithmetic, stated), which hurts once compute-bound
memory: Separate drafter (T5-small 77M / base 250M / large 800M for T5-XXL 11B) + its KV cache
accepted_tokens: not reported as tau; alpha 0.75-0.82 (T=0) / 0.62-0.71 (T=1) EnDe T5-XXL by drafter; CNN/DM 0.53-0.74; LaMDA 137B 0.57-0.75
speed: T5-XXL, 1 TPU-v4, bs1: EnDe 3.4x T=0 / 2.6x T=1 (T5-small, gamma 7); CNN/DM 3.1x / 2.3x (T5-small, gamma 5)
datasets: WMT EnDe, CNN/DM (T5); lm1b (GPT-like 97M); LaMDA 137B dialog (alpha only)

method: Independent derivation of lossless speculative sampling with a separately trained drafter
upside: Same draft-then-verify gain; works for greedy and nucleus sampling
method_downside: Drafter is a separate 4B model (8 layers, d=6144) trained for the target with the same tokenizer, with its own weights and KV; drafting is sequential so drafter latency grows with K; efficiency per step drops as K grows (stated)
memory: 4B drafter (~8 GB bf16, est.) + its KV cache; served on its own 16 TPU v4
quality: lossless (within hardware numerics); XSum ROUGE-2 0.156 vs 0.157 greedy; HumanEval 47.0% vs 45.1% nucleus
accepted_tokens: not reported
speed: Chinchilla 70B, 16 TPU v4, bs1, K=4: XSum 2.01x greedy, 1.92x nucleus; HumanEval 2.46x nucleus (14.1 -> 5.73 ms/token)
datasets: XSum, HumanEval

method: KD of drafter on on-policy (drafter-generated) data with divergence chosen per task (FKL/RKL/JSD/TVD)
upside: Aligns drafter to target distribution where drafter actually samples, raising block efficiency
method_downside: Training needs target logits for every drafter-generated token (target forward in the training loop); best divergence is task/decoding dependent, so per-setting tuning; drafter stays a separate model + KV
memory: Separate drafter (T5-Small 77M for T5-XL 3B; 33M for 234M decoder) + its KV
accepted_tokens: block efficiency (T5-Small -> T5-XL, greedy, gamma 7): XSum 2.68 -> 3.31; GSM8K 3.27 -> 4.14; CNN/DM 3.85 -> 4.83
speed: +10-45% over standard SD; e.g. CNN/DM greedy 2.07x -> 2.53x vs AR (T5-Small/T5-XL, TPUv4, bs1); lossy SD 6-10x latency cut
datasets: XSum, CNN/DM, WMT EnDe, GSM8K, LM1B, BigBenchHard (transfer)

method: Continually distill the drafter on live query traffic using verification results (rejected tokens)
upside: Drafter tracks the actual query distribution, raising acceptance without offline data collection
method_downside: Online training runs on serving GPUs (gradients, optimizer state, target logits buffer) and assumes idle compute; drafter weights change during serving, so behavior drifts and replicas can diverge; separate drafter + KV
memory: LLaMA-160M drafter + its KV + training state (grads, optimizer) on serving GPU (est.)
accepted_tokens: not reported as tau; token acceptance rate +0.1 to +0.65 (e.g. Spider 0.44 -> 0.76 per overview)
speed: 1.42-2.17x latency reduction (ICML/arXiv v4 abstract); hardware not captured
llama_results: Vicuna-7B target with LLaMA-160M drafter among pairs; per-model numbers not captured
datasets: Spider, GSM8K, Code-Search-Python, Alpaca-finance; T5 experiments

method: Pretrain 115M drafter, build distillation set from target generations, fine-tune with TVD++ loss
upside: Small dedicated drafter aligned to a chat-tuned target via a variance-reduced TV objective
method_downside: Drafter must be pretrained from scratch with target tokenizer (600B tokens, 32 A100) plus target-generated distillation data; separate model + KV; fine-tuned drafter loses to base drafter on OOD tasks (WMT18 DeEn, stated)
memory: 115M drafter (4 layers, d=1024) + its KV
accepted_tokens: block efficiency up to 2.3 (gamma=3, Llama 2 Chat 7B); CNN/DM 2.29 -> 2.4
speed: up to 2.4x vs AR, reported as MBSU (memory-bound speedup), not wall-clock
llama_results: Llama 2 Chat 7B: block eff. up to 2.3, up to 2.4x MBSU
datasets: Dolly-15k, XSum, CNN/DM

method: Selective KD: train a reference drafter, then distill only on top-k% tokens by loss gap (default k=0.4)
upside: Drafter spends its small capacity on tokens it can match, raising acceptance
method_downside: Needs an extra reference-model distillation run (two-phase training); drafter is trained on only ~40% of tokens, so it is deliberately weak on hard tokens; separate drafter + KV
memory: Separate drafter (Pythia-31M, CodeGen-350M, Qwen2.5-0.5B) + KV; reference model is training-only
accepted_tokens: not reported as tau; acceptance rate e.g. GSM8K 62.6% vs 57.6% (Pythia 31M->1.4B), MBPP 65.1% vs 49.9% (optimal)
speed: Pythia-31M->1.4B, A100, vLLM: MBPP 181.7 vs 149.2 tok/s (+22%), CNN/DM +14%, GSM8K +6% over DistillSpec
llama_results: EAGLE integration, Vicuna-7B-v1.3 MT-Bench: 63.48 -> 68.21 tok/s, acceptance 75.3% -> 76.3%
datasets: GSM8K, Alpaca, MBPP, CNN/DM, XSum; MT-Bench (EAGLE integration)

method: Log-linear laws for acceptance vs drafter pretraining tokens, capacity and batch; builds multi-layer EAGLE-style Scylla drafter
upside: Pretraining the drafter on ~10B tokens and adding layers raises acceptance well above EAGLE-2
method_downside: Bigger multi-layer drafter (up to 5 layers) costs more per draft step; needs ~10B-token drafter pretraining; EAGLE-style, so tied to target features and retrained per target
memory: 138M / 275M / 413M drafter (1/2/5 layers) + its KV
accepted_tokens: mean tau 6.32 (MT-Bench 6.45) vs EAGLE-2 3.94 (Vicuna-7B, T=0); Qwen2.5-7B 5.28 vs 4.05 (T=0)
speed: Qwen2.5-72B, 4x H800: bs1 250 vs 200 tok/s EAGLE-2 (AR 60); bs64 2150 vs 980 tok/s (AR 1763)
llama_results: mean tau T=0: Vicuna-7B 6.32; Llama2-Chat-70B 5.60 (EAGLE-2 4.17); Llama3-Instruct-8B 5.36 (EAGLE-2 4.18); T=1: L2-70B 5.54, L3-8B 4.97
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, Alpaca, CNN/DM, Natural Questions

method: K extra FFN heads on last hidden state predict t+2..t+K+1 independently; tree attention; Medusa-1 frozen, Medusa-2 joint
upside: No separate model or KV; heads reuse target features and train cheaply (5 h on A100 for 7B)
method_downside: Heads predict each offset independently, so later heads ignore earlier choices and acceptance decays with depth; each head has its own vocab-size projection; Medusa-2 changes backbone weights and typical acceptance is lossy
memory: not reported; each head = d x d ResBlock + d x V head, ~0.15B per head at 7B, ~0.74B for 5 heads (est.)
quality: lossless for Medusa-1 greedy; Medusa-2 / typical acceptance lossy: MT-Bench delta -0.14 (V13B) to +0.05 (V33B), Zephyr -0.07
accepted_tokens: acceleration rate 3.47 (Vicuna-7B), 3.51 (13B), 3.01 (33B), 3.14 (Zephyr-7B), Medusa-2
speed: Medusa-1 2.18x, Medusa-2 2.83x (Vicuna-7B, A100-80GB, bs1, MT-Bench); Zephyr-7B M2 2.66x
llama_results: Vicuna-7B M1 2.18x, M2 2.83x; Vicuna-13B M1 2.33x, M2 2.83x; Vicuna-33B M2 2.35x (MT-Bench, bs1)
datasets: MT-Bench (train: ShareGPT, UltraChat self-distill)

method: Draft heads conditioned on previously drafted tokens; Hydra++ adds 4-layer MLP heads, extra decoder layer, teacher distillation
upside: Sequential dependency fixes Medusa's independent-head problem, raising acceptance ~20%
method_downside: Heads run sequentially (one call per draft position; Hydra++ heads 0.6-1.4 ms each vs Medusa 0.3 ms), so drafting latency grows with depth; Hydra++ prefix attention layer adds its own KV cache; retrained per target
memory: not reported; larger than Medusa heads (4-layer MLP per head + 1 decoder layer ~0.2B at 7B, est.)
quality: lossless (greedy); typical sampling eps=0.15 matches base quality (stated)
accepted_tokens: Hydra++ tau 3.70 (Vicuna-7B), 3.72 (13B), 3.62 (33B), MT-Bench greedy
speed: Hydra++ 2.70x vs AR, 1.27x vs Medusa (Vicuna-7B, A100-40GB, bs1, MT-Bench); SpecBench avg 2.17x vs Medusa 1.75x; gap to Medusa shrinks at bs8 (fig.)
datasets: MT-Bench; SpecBench (MT chat, translation, summarization, QA, math, RAG)

method: One-layer AR drafter over target second-to-top features plus token shifted one step; static tree
upside: Drafter reads target features, so one small layer suffices; feature-level AR resolves sampling uncertainty
method_downside: Needs target hidden states each round, so drafting cannot start before verification ends; drafter has its own (1-layer) KV cache; retrained per target (and per fine-tune)
memory: 0.24B / 0.37B / 0.56B / 0.99B drafter for 7B/13B/33B/70B (0.28B Mixtral) + 1-layer KV
accepted_tokens: tau 3.98 (Vicuna-13B, T=0, MT-Bench), 3.20 at T=1; 3.81 (LLaMA2-Chat-70B, T=0)
speed: ~2.8-3.0x MT-Bench T=0 bs1 (figure); HumanEval 3.33-3.76x; throughput 1.97x (Vicuna-7B, bs8, RTX 3090), 1.99x (L2-70B, bs5, 4x A100-40G)
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, Alpaca

method: Context-aware dynamic draft tree using drafter confidence as acceptance proxy; reranking; reuses EAGLE drafter
upside: Spends draft budget where acceptance is likely; no retraining over EAGLE
method_downside: Relies on drafter being well calibrated (stated); tree shape changes per step, which breaks static CUDA graphs and batching; still needs target features and per-target drafter
memory: same as EAGLE (reuses EAGLE drafter, 0.24B for 7B) + 1-layer KV
accepted_tokens: tau 4.83 MT-Bench, mean 4.65 (Vicuna-13B, T=0); mean 4.40 at T=1
speed: 4.26x MT-Bench, 4.04x mean (Vicuna-13B, T=0, bs1); 3.80x mean at T=1; hardware not stated
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, Alpaca, CNN/DM, Natural Questions

method: Direct token prediction (no feature loss), fused low/mid/high target features, training-time test
upside: Fused multi-layer features plus training on its own outputs let acceptance keep scaling with training data
method_downside: Needs low/mid/high hidden states from the target each round, so drafter is tied to target internals and retrained per target; training-time test multiplies training cost; gain collapses at batch ~56 as verification becomes compute-bound
memory: not reported; ~0.4B for 8B target (1 decoder layer + 3d->d fusion FC + 32k draft-vocab head, est.) + 1-layer KV
speed: 5.58x (Vicuna-13B, bs1, T=0); vLLM 1.75x bs2 -> 1.01x bs56 (chain 2, no tree)
llama_results: T=0: Vicuna-13B 5.58x, LLaMA-3.1-8B 4.40x, LLaMA-3.3-70B 4.11x, R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B 4.05x; T=1 3.07x (L3.1-8B)
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, Alpaca, CNN/DM

method: Top-K ranking distillation plus multi-step context alignment (train on drafter's own features) over EAGLE-2
upside: Drafter sees its own features in training, reducing train/inference mismatch at no inference cost
method_downside: Multi-step (n=3) alignment costs n times EAGLE training (stated); needs target top-K logits during training; inherits EAGLE-2 per-target drafter and target-feature dependency
memory: same as EAGLE-2 drafter (~0.24B for 7B, est.) + 1-layer KV
accepted_tokens: tau 5.08 (LLaMA3-Instruct-8B, T=0); 5.58 (LLaMA2-Chat-13B, T=0)
speed: 4.05x (LLaMA3-Instruct-70B, H800, bs1, T=0, mean of 3 sets); T=1 3.85x
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K (README DeepSeek runs add Alpaca, QA, Summarization)

method: Token-alignable training (mask misaligned tokens) plus draft model with token-guided fusion and token-enhanced head
upside: Fixes feature/token misalignment between training and decoding, lengthening accepted drafts
method_downside: Larger drafter than EAGLE (TGF expanded to 11008, dual heads); multi-step training (150-600 A100-h vs HASS 130-500); masking removes loss signal on misaligned (hard) tokens
memory: 0.41B / 0.42B / 0.65B / 2.07B drafter for 7B/8B/13B/70B + its KV
accepted_tokens: tau 5.38 mean / 4.85 MT-Bench (LLaMA3-Instruct-8B, T=0); 5.20 mean at T=1
speed: 3.35x mean (LLaMA3-8B, A100 80G, bs1, T=0); vLLM chain-2: 1.52x bs2 -> 1.25x bs16; README claims up to 4.2x
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K (also Qwen2-7B, Mixtral-8x7B in NeurIPS ver.)

method: Semi-AR drafter (k tokens per pass) with coupled sequential glancing distillation; custom decoding tree
upside: Fewer drafter passes per draft block than a pure AR drafter
method_downside: Tokens inside a block are predicted without seeing each other, lowering acceptance (stated; CSGD only partly fixes it); ~2-layer drafter heavier than EAGLE's; needs target features, retrained per target
memory: not reported as count; drafter 'comparable to two Transformer layers' (2 LSTM + attention + MLP), ~0.4B for 7B (est.) + KV
accepted_tokens: tau 3.34 / 3.88 / 3.70 (Vicuna-7B, MT-Bench/HumanEval/GSM8K, T=0)
llama_results: T=0 MT-Bench: Vicuna-7B 3.10x/3.34; V13B 2.97x/3.37; L2-Chat-7B 2.94x/2.82; L2-13B 3.11x/2.95 (HumanEval up to 3.51x)
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K

method: RNN drafter conditioned on target hidden states; beam search drafting; dynamic tree attention dedups prefixes; KD from target
upside: Tiny recurrent drafter is cheap per step and runs on-device (MLX)
method_downside: Beam search (width up to 45) multiplies drafter and verification work, which hurts at batch>1; needs target hidden states; non-greedy implementation may not match the distribution exactly (README)
memory: not reported (one-layer RNN + few MLP layers drafter, + per-beam state)
quality: lossless (stated); README notes T>0 implementation may not match distribution
accepted_tokens: tau 4.20 (Vicuna-7B), 4.21 (13B), 3.87 (33B), MT-Bench greedy
speed: 2.80x (Vicuna-7B/13B, H100, PyTorch, bs1, greedy); MLX up to 2.3x M2 Ultra, 1.37x M1 Max; bs80 BW2 ~1636 tok/s total (H100, 7B)
datasets: MT-Bench, AlpacaEval

method: Sampling-free draft-tree reward plus group-based policy optimization of the drafter
upside: Training objective matches tree decoding, so drafter optimizes accepted length of the tree, not per-token loss
method_downside: Training builds and evaluates grouped draft trees (two phases, 200-900 GPU-h, stated); reward is tied to one tree policy; starts from an EAGLE-3 drafter, so inherits its target-feature dependency and per-target retraining
memory: same as EAGLE-3 drafter (initialized from it); no extra inference memory
accepted_tokens: tau 6.52 (LLaMA-3.1-8B, T=0) vs EAGLE-3 6.07
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K

method: Hybrid KL + total-variation loss with adaptive schedule, directly optimizing acceptance rate
upside: Loss targets acceptance itself, helping low-capacity drafters most; drop-in for any drafter type
method_downside: TV term needs the full target distribution per training token; objective models chain sampling, not tree verification; fixed per-head aggregation and scheduler hyperparameters (stated)
memory: none beyond the drafter it trains (EAGLE-3, Medusa, MLP speculator, MTP)
accepted_tokens: tau 3.84 vs 3.75 KL (LLaMA-3.1-8B EAGLE-3, T=0, MT-Bench, chain); 3.48 vs 3.39 at T=1
speed: 2.62x MT-Bench, 3.35x HumanEval (LLaMA-3.1-8B EAGLE-3, vLLM 0.11, bs1, T=0); hardware not stated
llama_results: LLaMA-3.1-8B EAGLE-3: tau 3.84 (T=0), 2.62x MT-Bench; MLP speculator HumanEval tau 2.42 -> 2.83; LLaMA-3.3-70B EAGLE-3 mean tau 4.81 T=0 (+0.5%), 4.66 T=1 (+3.5%)
datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K

method: On-policy distillation with target-assisted rollouts, error-position replay, acceptance-aware loss weighting
upside: Drafter trains on its own rollouts, closing exposure bias at deep positions
method_downside: Training needs the target in the loop for rollouts (verl RL stack, ~120 H200 GPU-h for Qwen3-4B); per-target retraining; main recipe is on a DFlash block drafter, so inherits its target-feature dependency
memory: not reported as count; 5-layer drafter for 4B/8B targets (8 layers for 30B), same as base drafter
accepted_tokens: tau 5.96 (Qwen3-4B, T=0 thinking); 5.73 (Qwen3-8B); 5.13/5.05 at T=0.6
speed: mean 4.86x (Qwen3-4B, T=0 thinking), 4.89x (Qwen3-8B); H200, bs1
datasets: GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME25, MBPP, HumanEval, SWE-Lite, MT-Bench

method: Simulate target verification at each training step; accept/reject patterns supervise via verification head and per-position weights
upside: Drafter learns where verification actually rejects, raising accepted length at no inference cost
method_downside: Supervision comes from simulated verification against the target's outputs, so the drafter is tied to that target and acceptance rule and retrained per target; inherits base drafter's target-feature dependency
memory: none beyond base drafter (EAGLE-3 or DFlash); verification head training-only
accepted_tokens: tau 6.78 vs 6.28 (Qwen3-4B EAGLE-3, T=0); DFlash 6.08 vs 5.73
speed: 4.39x vs 4.07x (Qwen3-4B EAGLE-3, A100 80GB, bf16, HF Transformers, T=0); DFlash 4.81x vs 4.54x
datasets: GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME25, HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, MT-Bench, Alpaca

method: Online learning (dynamic regret) evolves drafters from verification feedback; Ens-EAGLE(-3), Opt-Hydra, Online-LR
upside: Drafter adapts to live traffic with a regret bound linked to speedup
method_downside: Ens-EAGLE keeps N drafter copies (N=3 in experiments) with different learning rates (memory xN); online updates need training compute and the drafter drifts during serving; Online-LR variant is step-level and lossy
memory: Ens: 3 drafter copies + optimizer state (not quantified); Opt-Hydra: Hydra heads + momentum state
quality: lossless (token-level variants); Online-LR lossy (Qwen3-8B MMLU 84.52% vs target 83.81%)
accepted_tokens: tau 2.70 (Opt-Hydra, Vicuna-7B, Alpaca-finance); 2.94 (Llama-2-7B-Chat, GSM8K); 2.01 (Ens-EAGLE, Vicuna-7B, GSM8K)
speed: vs vanilla SD (not AR): Opt-Hydra 1.18-1.55x (Vicuna-7B), 1.61-2.03x (Llama-2-7B-Chat); 4x A800 80GB

datasets: GSM8K, MATH, MMLU (math subset), Code-Search-Python, Spider, MBPP, Alpaca-finance

method: Drafter split into frozen shared and trainable private MoE experts; regenerate data with fine-tuned target; select high-value samples
upside: Re-aligns a drafter to a fine-tuned target with 27.5% of params and ~61% of retrain cost
method_downside: MoE drafter (shared + private experts + router) is larger than a plain EAGLE drafter; still needs the fine-tuned target to regenerate data and retrain the private part per fine-tune
memory: ~462 MB drafter params (full retrain), 127 MB trainable private part (27.5%)
accepted_tokens: tau 5.19 vs 4.69 full FT (Qwen2.5-Math-7B, T=0); 5.18 vs 4.59 (Coder-7B); 4.21 vs 3.89 (Meditron3-Qwen2.5-7B)
speed: 3.27x vs 3.07x full FT (Math-7B, T=0); Coder 3.11x vs 2.76x; 4x H200 stated (other extract gave 3.06x; numbers conflict)

method: Draft by skipping ~half of target layers (attn+MLP set found by Bayesian optimization); full model verifies
upside: No extra model or training; draft shares weights and KV with target
method_downside: Draft still runs ~50% of target depth per token, capping speedup; skip set searched offline per model (BO, 1000 iters, ~2.5 h 13B, ~6 h 70B) and static, so it degrades under task shift
memory: none (shared weights and KV; authors: no extra memory)
quality: lossless (ROUGE-2 0.108 vs 0.106 LLaMA-2-13B CNN/DM; Pass@1 0.317 vs 0.311 CodeLLaMA-13B)
accepted_tokens: acceptance ~0.92 (LLaMA-2-13B CNN/DM, greedy), 0.85-0.92 across LLaMA-2; tau not reported
speed: 1.22-1.99x (A100 40/80GB, HF transformers 4.33, bs1, greedy; T=0.2/0.6 sampling also tested); best 1.99x LLaMA-2-70B CNN/DM
datasets: CNN/DM, XSum, HumanEval (GSM8K, MT-Bench in later version)

method: Train with layer dropout + shared early-exit loss; early layers draft, remaining layers verify
upside: Draft and verifier share weights, LM head and KV cache, so no auxiliary model
method_downside: Needs layer-dropout/early-exit (continual) pretraining that changes base weights; draft quality capped by shallow exit layer; later fine-tuning can break exits
memory: none extra (single model, shared exit LM head; draft KV and hidden states reused by verify)
quality: lossless vs the LayerSkip-trained model; trained model has minimal last-layer accuracy drop vs original (continual pretraining)
accepted_tokens: token acceptance 68.9% Llama2-7B / 74.5% 13B CNN/DM (E=8, d=12, continual PT); 77.8% 7B from scratch; 45% Llama1-7B HumanEval; tau not reported
speed: up to 2.16x CNN/DM (Llama2-7B, scratch PT), 1.82x HumanEval (A100), 2.0x TOPv2; H100, greedy, max 512 tokens, bs1

datasets: CNN/DM, XSum, HumanEval, TOPv2 (+ MMLU, NaturalQuestions etc. for last-layer accuracy)

method: Fixed shallow sub-network (layer 2-3) + trained 1-attention adapter drafts; second early exit stops drafting on low confidence
upside: Tiny adapter (67M vs Medusa 591M) reuses target's shallow layers and KV
method_downside: Adapter trained per target; draft quality capped by fixed shallow exit layer; drafting still runs the shallow sub-network sequentially per token
memory: 67M adapter (Vicuna-7B; 88.7% fewer than Medusa 591M) + its 1-layer KV
accepted_tokens: compression rate 1.41-2.22 by Spec-Bench subtask (Vicuna-7B)
speed: avg 1.50x Vicuna-7B (1.24x translation to 1.68x MT-Bench), 1.44x Vicuna-13B (V100; bs and temperature not stated; exit l=2/3, eta 0.6, gamma 6)

method: On-the-fly optimization of skipped-layer set from current context + confidence-based draft stopping; no training
upside: Plug-and-play; adapts skip set to task without offline search
method_downside: Skip-set optimization phase at inference (~2 min) and task-dependent sparsity; draft keeps ~half of layers so speedup capped; small models have little layer redundancy
memory: none (shared weights and KV)
accepted_tokens: mean generated length M 4.34 CNN/DM, 3.13 GSM8K, 8.21 TinyStories (LLaMA-2-13B, greedy); 3.85/2.99/6.17 (LLaMA-2-70B); 4.75 CodeLLaMA-13B HumanEval
llama_results: LLaMA-2-13B 1.28-1.53x (1.37x CNN/DM, 1.31x GSM8K, 1.53x TinyStories); LLaMA-2-70B 1.39-1.62x; CodeLLaMA-13B/34B tested
datasets: CNN/DM, GSM8K, TinyStories, HumanEval, WMT16 De-En

method: Re-select skipped layers every step via dynamic programming over hidden states from the last verify pass; no training
upside: Skip set tracks the context each step instead of a static or per-task set
method_downside: Per-step DP adds latency that eats most of the gain on small models (1.24x at 8B); depends on last verify's hidden states so drafting waits for verification; draft still deep
memory: none extra beyond cached hidden states of last verify (est.)
datasets: Spec-Bench (MT-Bench, translation, summarization, QA, math, RAG)

method: Picks exit layer and speculation length per context from tracked per-layer acceptance in LayerSkip-style self-SD
upside: Adapts draft depth and length to context with negligible runtime overhead
method_downside: Needs LayerSkip early-exit-trained checkpoints; exit choice relies on running acceptance stats, so it degrades on out-of-distribution prompts
memory: 0.52-2.26% memory overhead (avg 1.54%)

method_downside: Needs early-exit-trained models; tentatively accepted tokens can still be rolled back at final verification (wasted work); four coupled knobs (Nd, Ni, Ld, Li)

method: Drafter predicts verification outcomes and pre-builds next speculation for each; fallback to SD on miss
upside: on a cache hit the next draft is ready, removing drafting latency from the critical path
method_downside: needs a dedicated draft GPU; speculations for missed outcomes are wasted compute; cache misses rise with batch size (at bs16 a fast backup speculator beats the neural one)
memory: 1B drafter on separate H100 + speculation cache O(BFK(K+1)(V+1)) bits, 'hundreds of MB' (stated)
accepted_tokens: not reported as tau (cache hit rate ~80-90% at fan-out 128, T=0)
speed: 4.68x avg vs AR, 1.58x vs SD (Llama-3.1-70B on 4x H100 + 1B draft on 1x H100, bs1, T=0): 255.8 vs 161.8 SD vs 54.7 AR tok/s; Qwen3-32B 2.29x
llama_results: Llama-3.1-70B + Llama-3.2-1B: 5.17x HumanEval, 5.50x GSM8K, 4.10x Alpaca, 3.93x UltraFeedback, 4.68x avg vs AR
datasets: HumanEval, Alpaca, GSM8K, UltraFeedback

method: Chain of >2 models (target, 4-bit copy of target, EAGLE-2 drafter) with optimal-time theorem
upside: cheap intermediate verifier filters drafts so the target verifies long accepted runs
method_downside: 3 models resident with 3 KV caches whose footprint grows with length, lowering gains on summarization/RAG (stated); conditions for >3 models hard to meet with off-the-shelf models (stated)
memory: not reported; full 4-bit (group 128) copy of target + EAGLE-2 head + their KV (est.)
accepted_tokens: 9.88 (Vicuna-7B), 9.84 (LLaMA2-7B), 9.44 (LLaMA3-8B), 9.32 (Qwen2-7B) tokens per target pass, Spec-Bench overall; 7.48 LLaMA2-70B; T not stated
speed: 3.48x Vicuna-7B overall (up to 4.43x Math); 3.66x LLaMA2-7B; A800-80G; T not stated
llama_results: LLaMA2-7B 3.31-4.10x (3.66x overall); LLaMA3-8B 2.71-3.87x (3.31x); Vicuna-7B 3.48x; Vicuna-13B 2.69x; LLaMA2-70B 2.92x
datasets: Spec-Bench (MT, translation, summarization, QA, math, RAG)

method: Fixes ragged-tensor desync in batch SD (EqSpec); regroups same-length sequences across batches (ExSpec)
upside: keeps position IDs, masks and KV in sync when sequences accept different counts
method_downside: unpad-realign-repad overhead grows superlinearly (39.4% of compute at bs8, 46.7% at bs16); beyond bs8 cross-batch grouping fails more often and falls back to realignment; static batching only
memory: drafter (68M or 0.6B) + its KV; padding overhead not reported
quality: 90-97% exact output match vs AR at greedy (95-98% partial match); residual attributed to FP nondeterminism
accepted_tokens: not reported
speed: EqSpec 2.4-2.6x at bs4, ExSpec 2.8-3.0x at bs8 throughput vs bs1 (A100-80GB, greedy, 5 draft tokens, HF Transformers 4.51.3)
llama_results: Vicuna-7B/68M: 2.6x (EqSpec, bs4), 2.8x (ExSpec, bs8) vs bs1; baselines BSP 0.2-3.5%, DSD ~0% exact match
datasets: SpecBench, Multi30k

method: Long-context large-batch decode is KV-bound, so sparse-KV self-spec (StreamingLLM/SnapKV) or small drafts help
upside: draft cost uses a fixed small KV budget while target KV load dominates, so SD speeds up even at high throughput
method_downside: only helps once context is long enough for KV to dominate; tighter draft KV budget lowers acceptance; standalone drafter adds weights and full KV
memory: self-spec: draft KV budget 256-512 (StreamingLLM) or ~2K (SnapKV) tokens/seq, no extra weights; standalone drafter can take 38-140% of target memory (stated)
accepted_tokens: expected tokens/step 2.53-5.61 across configs (latest version); SnapKV drafts accept far more than StreamingLLM
speed: up to 2.51x LLaMA-3.1-8B (SnapKV self-spec, 100K ctx, bs41, 8x H100, greedy); 1.2-1.7x StreamingLLM self-spec at bs32-128, 8K-32K ctx (A100/H100/L40)
llama_results: LLaMA-3.1-8B up to 2.51x (SnapKV); LLaMA-2-7B-32K 1.27-1.69x (8x A100, v1), 1.68x bs64 8K ctx
datasets: PG-19, RULER (QA-1, CWE, needle-in-haystack)

method: On vLLM: load/SLO-adaptive draft length, confidence-prior verifier, SLO-aware efficiency estimator
upside: speculation length shrinks under load and grows when idle, so SD does not hurt SLOs
method_downside: adaptive length relies on noisy pre-verification acceptance estimates; per-step estimator/scheduler overhead
memory: drafter 68M / 160M / 1B + KV
quality: lossless (acceptance still by target distribution, stated)
accepted_tokens: not reported
speed: 1.1-1.8x vs AR across 15 setups (1x L40, 1/2/4/8x A800, vLLM); 10-61% over other methods' speedup; abstract 1.14-14.3x is vs other speculative systems, not AR
llama_results: Llama-3.1-70B + Llama-3.2-1B on 8x A800; Vicuna-7B/68M (L40, A800), Vicuna-33B/160M (2-4x A800); per-model numbers in figures
datasets: Azure LLM inference traces (code, conversation), Mooncake trace (v1); BurstGPT in v2

method: L = C1/(1 - RPS*C2), with SD costs split into prefill, draft, verify given acceptance and draft length
upside: explains from first principles why SD speedup shrinks as server load rises
method_downside: acceptance is an exogenous constant per token (independent of earlier rejections), so tree or verifier choices cannot be modeled; models mean latency only, valid before saturation
memory: none (analysis)
quality: n/a (analysis; acceptance forced by overriding rejection sampler)
accepted_tokens: acceptance set to 50-100%, draft length 1-10 (synthetic)
speed: no new speedup; SD speedup erodes with load when C2 ratio >1, faster for longer drafts (vLLM 0.13.0, 1x A100; 4x A100 for 70B)
llama_results: Llama-3.1-8B (1x A100) and 70B (4x A100) verifiers with EAGLE-3-style drafter, Llama-3.1-8B drafter for 70B; no speedup numbers; also Qwen3 8B-235B, gpt-oss-20b
datasets: synthetic prompts from Pride and Prejudice; prefill/decode 256-1024; GuideLLM load sweep
